A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ArabCulture study. Their complete main text, figures, tables and Appendices A-D support reliable comparison after matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original LLM benchmark results, a 200-example manual explanation evaluation, and experiments with cultural context augmentation (Sections 4-5 and Appendix D).

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds evaluations of three reasoning models in Tables 3 and 9.

M1.justification: Dataset construction, validation, task formulation and GPT-4o context augmentation remain unchanged. The additional models are evaluated comparators.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 3,482 MSA instances covering 13 countries, 12 domains and 54 subtopics, with the same tasks and scenarios. Figure 1 replaces illustrative examples without changing demonstrated dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 3 and 9 add DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama (70B), DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen (32B) and QwQ (32B). This extends the existing comparison with a reasoning-model group while retaining all previous comparators.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix C retain English and Arabic prompts, completion and MCQ scoring, zero-temperature settings, and three location-context levels. No separate or revised testing procedure is specified for the added models.

E4.justification: The country/topic breakdowns, country-specificity analysis, 200-example explanation evaluation and six-model context-augmentation study remain unchanged, including their appendix results and Figures 3-4.

E5.justification: Both versions report point accuracies without repeated-run summaries, confidence intervals or significance tests. No seed information or uncertainty-estimation procedure is added or revised.

E6.justification: Tables 3 and 9 add scores for the three reasoning models. For example, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen obtains 34.3% MCQ accuracy at every location level in both prompt languages. All matched pre-existing numerical results and plotted findings remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Task/category definitions and location-context notation remain unchanged. Neither version contains formal theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same benchmark contribution, coverage claims, and conclusions about cultural variation and difficulties for open-weight models up to 32B parameters.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 newly interprets reasoning models' weak cultural-task scores as suggesting challenges fundamentally different from mathematics and programming. Existing interpretations and limitations concerning dialects, location leakage and geographic coverage are retained.

D1.justification: Annotation instructions, evaluation-framework disclosure, prompt templates and dataset-access information remain unchanged. New institutional acknowledgments provide no concrete implementation settings or hardware configuration.

R1.justification: v2 adds the DeepSeek-R1 reference and removes Liang et al. (2024), citing Huang et al. (2024) for AceGPT-v2 instead. Broader research positioning is retained; several other reference edits update publication metadata.

P1.justification: Limited edits correct an author name, update affiliations, rephrase Appendix C-D prose and add acknowledgments. The main narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn and replaces mixed-topic examples with lunch examples from Algeria, Egypt, Syria and KSA. Tables 3 and 9 gain model rows, and several existing figures and appendix tables move; the other figure contents are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added reasoning-model comparisons provide a useful check of a previously unevaluated model class under the benchmark's existing protocol, modestly extending the empirical evidence. The gains are limited: the broader interpretation about fundamentally different reasoning challenges is not separately tested, and Sections 4.1 and 6 still report 31 models despite the expanded 34-model tables.
